top_story.headline: FEC flags four committees over apparent unauthorized spending, including $13,064.50 in “misappropriations” recoveries at a Seafarers PAC
top_story.dek: Letters dated October 6 and 8 say the Commission may take further legal action over what it calls apparent improper use of committee funds.
paragraphs: The Federal Election Commission asked Seafarers Political Activity Donation - Seafarers International Union of North America about a $13,064.50 receipt on its September Monthly report labeled “Insurance recovery for additional misappropriations found See memo.” The letter, filed October 8, calls the item an apparent unauthorized use of committee funds and says the Commission “may take further legal action regarding this apparent improper use of Committee funds.” Seafarers letter.

The same day, the Commission sent EchoStar Corporation and DISH Network Corporation PAC a letter about a $4,767.41 disbursement labeled “DISPUTED ACH DEBIT” with the same warning, and Bish for Congress (Republican challenger Christine S. Bish) one about disbursements described as fraud charges ($483.27 and $1,000.00, noted as reported to Wells Fargo) plus Wells Fargo provisional credits of $5,001.21 and $6,192.30 that it must tie to specific expenditures. EchoStar letter; Bish letter.

Earlier, in a letter filed October 6, James Osyf for Congress (Democratic challenger James Osyf in Virginia) was asked about a $2,058.01 disbursement labeled “Unauthorized transaction” on its July Quarterly report; the Commission noted the committee’s explanation but also said it may take further legal action. Osyf letter.

sections.headline: 22 FEC information requests and one termination hit sitting members’ campaigns
paragraphs: The Federal Election Commission sent 22 Requests for Additional Information to 15 campaign committees of sitting members of Congress, and approved the termination of one more. Most are template notices about excessive contributions, missing 48-hour notices, joint-fundraising paperwork and summary-page math; one asks Rep. Eric Swalwell’s committee for more on “Uncashed Checks” adjustments tied to a Form 99 it filed July 15, 2026.

sections.headline: 56 PACs and party committees were asked to fix or explain their reports
paragraphs: Many of the PAC and party letters are paperwork fixes (unsigned reports, bad totals, Statement of Organization problems). The standouts are two letters about apparent unauthorized disbursements (to the Seafarers committee and the EchoStar committee), a union PAC’s $20,863.51 “deposit made in error” refund, a $10,860.00 voided independent-expenditure check, and a Maine Republican Party transfer of $10,000.00 to a non-federal account.

items: AB PAC — RFAI on August Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Possible late 24-hour reports for last-minute independent expenditures, including $181,022.00 to “K Squared Media LLC” on 8/4/26 supporting Sen. Dan Sullivan, and a dissemination date that doesn’t match. Filing.

Filing.

Greenberg Traurig, P.A. PAC — RFAI on Amended July Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Amended report shows $13,120.72 more in receipts than the original. Filing.
Halff Associates FED PAC — RFAI on October Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent named on the committee’s Statement of Organization. Filing.
Hispanic Political Action Coalition HISPAC — RFAI on Statement of Organization (filed 10/08): The Statement of Organization lacks a mailing address for the campaign depository (Line 9). Filing.
Independence Blue Cross LLC PAC — RFAI on Amended August Monthly Report (filed 10/08): Contributions the committee gave to candidates appear to exceed the $5,000-per-election limit. Filing.

Indivisible Action — RFAI on August Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Year-to-date per-election totals for Colorado Senate, Minnesota Senate and New York’s 10th Congressional District look wrong, Schedule E is missing required details, and 24/48-hour reports naming “Civitech,” “Good Influence,” “Scale to Win” and “Taskforce+” show dates that don’t match the report. Filing.

International Association of Heat and Frost Insulators and Asbestos Workers Local No. 1 PAC — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report was not signed by the treasurer on file and lacks its Detailed Summary Page. Filing.

Jewelers of America, Inc. Political Action Committee (JAPAC) — RFAI on October Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): Contributions to candidates for the 2026 primary were paid after that primary, the report put candidate contributions on the wrong line, and candidate-committee recipients need full names and addresses. Filing.
Leadership for Ohio Fund — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent named on the committee’s Statement of Organization. Filing.

Lennox Employee Advocacy Program Lennox International Inc — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Opening cash does not match the prior report’s closing balance; cycle-to-date (Column B) totals on Lines 6(c), 7, 17, 19, 20, 29, 31, and 32 of the summary pages do not equal the prior report plus this report. Filing.
MAHA PAC — RFAI on September Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Independent expenditures (attached) may have been reported late on 24-hour reports. Filing.

MAHA PAC — RFAI on Amended May Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): A 48-hour-reported independent expenditure supporting Rep. Julia Letlow ($22,433.67 to “JLK Strategies, LLC” on 4/4/26) is not itemized on Schedule E. Filing.

MAHA PAC — RFAI on Amended June Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): A 24-hour-reported independent expenditure supporting Rep. Julia Letlow ($22,649.06 to “JLK Strategies, LLC” on 5/4/26) is not itemized on Schedule E, and cycle-to-date totals on Line 29 are off. Filing.

Maine Republican Party — RFAI on August Monthly Report (filed 10/08): The Xerox Financial Services debt was omitted, a $10,000.00 transfer to a non-federal account needs explaining, and Schedule H4 reimbursements to individuals of $2,171.63 don’t match their memo entries. Filing.

Monroe Township Republican Executive Committee — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent named on the committee’s Statement of Organization. Filing.

Montana Republican State Central Committee — RFAI on September Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Cycle-to-date (Column B) totals on Lines 21(a)(i), 21(a)(ii), 21(b) and 32 don’t add up. Filing.

Montana Voters PAC — RFAI on Amended 30 Day Post-General Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Amended post-general report for 2024 shows $150,000 more in receipts than the original. Filing.
New Voice PAC — RFAI on Amended July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report shows contributions from another political committee that appear to exceed the $5,000-per-year limit. Filing.

Old North Leadership PAC — RFAI on Amended Statement of Organization (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Asked to clarify its relationship with “Rouzer Congressional Trust,” which appears to be a joint fundraising representative; if this committee is a participant, its Statement of Organization must say so. Filing.

Oregonians for Common Sense PAC — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent named on the committee’s Statement of Organization. Filing.

Pictsweet Company Good Government Committee — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): The report was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent named on the committee’s Statement of Organization. Filing.
Project 218 — RFAI on September Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Ending cash on hand (Line 8) does not equal the closing calendar-year-to-date cash figure. Filing.

Republican Mainstreet Partnership PAC — RFAI on September Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Cycle-to-date totals on Lines 21(b), 21(c) and 23 are off, contributions it received appear to exceed the $5,000-per-year limit, and contributions it gave to candidates appear to exceed $5,000 per election. Filing.

Reviving American Jobs Again PAC DBA Equal Opportunity Now — RFAI on August Monthly Report (filed 10/08): Contributions from, and to, other political committees appear to exceed the $5,000 limits. Filing.

Road Sprinkler Fitters Local Union No. 669, UA, AFL-CIO PAC — RFAI on June Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Asked about $20,863.51 paid to the committee’s own union sponsor as a “Refund of contribution (deposit made in error)”; the FEC wants the original deposit date and, if the money came in by mistake, the original receipt disclosed, noting corporate and union money cannot fund federal elections. Filing.
SC Rising — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Independent expenditures described as “MESSAGIG TO SUPPORT” and similar need clearer purposes. Filing.

Seafarers Political Activity Donation - Seafarers International Union of Na-Agliw — RFAI on September Monthly Report (filed 10/08): Asked about a $13,064.50 receipt labeled “Insurance recovery for additional misappropriations found,” which the FEC says looks like apparent unauthorized use of committee funds; the FEC says it may still take further legal action. Filing.
Southern California Pipe Trades District Council 16 Federal PAC — RFAI on Amended 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (filed 10/08): Amended report shows $26,207.02 more in receipts than the original. Filing.

The Equity Alliance Fund Action PAC — RFAI on June Monthly Report (filed 10/08): The report shows voided contributions for independent expenditures totaling $10,860.00; if a check was never cashed it should be a negative entry on Schedule E, not a receipt. Filing.

UA Local 85 Political Action Committee — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The report shows interest from “Huntington Bank,” a depository not listed on the Statement of Organization. Filing.

Vanteo, LLC Political Action Committee — RFAI on Amended July Monthly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Amended report shows $21,000 more in disbursements than the original. Filing.

Vote Rev PAC — RFAI on July Quarterly Report (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): A “Reimbursement of Administrative Expenses” to “Vote Rev,” an apparently unregistered organization, looks like an in-kind contribution because another entity paid the original bills. Filing.

Western Alliance of Farmworker Advocates PAC (WAFA PAC) — RFAI on Amended Statement of Organization (filed 10/06; not picked up in earlier editions): Statement of Organization checks the “separate segregated fund” box but names no connected corporation, union or trade association; it must name the connected organization or change the committee type. Filing.

Western and Southern Life Insurance Co Political Action Committee (Western-Southern PAC) — RFAI on Amended Statement of Organization (filed 10/07; not picked up in earlier editions): Statement of Organization checks the “separate segregated fund” box but names no connected corporation, union or trade association; it must name the connected organization or change the committee type. Filing.

Young People for a New Era — RFAI on Amended July Quarterly Report (filed 10/08): The amended report shows $18,516.17 more in disbursements than the original, and the FEC wants an explanation for why it was not disclosed originally; asked why independent expenditures appear without the required 24-hour reports. Filing.

sections.headline: No Form 99 correspondence beyond terminations
paragraphs: Every new Form 99 in this window was a Termination Approval; there were no Miscellaneous Submissions, debt-settlement responses or loan-forgiveness filings.

sections.headline: 50 termination approvals, mostly House candidate committees
